rundown: RedHawks beat Cougars 106-45 at Millett Hall in Oxford, OH in front of 1,711. RedHawks led 55-25 at the half and never looked back. The 1st quarter decided it: RedHawks won it 30-13. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 100%).
Leading the way — Cougars: Maggie Stephenson 16 pts; Elly Daniels 1 ast, 4 reb. RedHawks: Amber Tretter 16 pts; Julianna LaMendola 7 ast; Núria Jurjo 8 reb.
Where RedHawks won it: they shot 61% to 36%, shot 41% from three to 29% and won the boards 39-28.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 11, 10:28 AM ET. It had Cougars 20% and RedHawks 80%, projecting Cougars 62.9 – RedHawks 73.9 (136.8 total, RedHawks by 11).

Final: Cougars 45 – RedHawks 106. Right winner: it had RedHawks at 80%.

Thin data: 3 of 6 key inputs were sourced (missing: MVNU pts scored, MVNU pts allowed, MVNU lineup rating or past seasons), so league averages filled the gaps. It was logged as a no-data call: graded and learned from, never offered as a bet.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Cougars came in with a league-average attack and a league-average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 14 and 14 games of evidence. Projected to score 62.9, they scored 45 (−17.9 points, 28% under); projected to allow 73.9, they allowed 106 (+32.1 points, 43% over).

RedHawks came in with a league-average attack and a 8% stingier than average defense (3-0, 75.3 scored and 47 allowed a game over 3 games), worth about 160 and 159 games of evidence. Projected to score 73.9, they scored 106 (+32.1 points, 43% over); projected to allow 62.9, they allowed 45 (−17.9 points, 28% under).

The bigger miss was RedHawks' scoring (+32.1 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 151 against 136.8 projected (+14.2), about the 85th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14).

Margin: RedHawks by 61 against RedHawks by 11 projected, about the 99th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±13).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (MVNU pts scored, MVNU pts allowed, MVNU lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.105 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +51.3 points. It counts toward NCAAW scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections (it's how teams with no standings on the routes build a record of their own).

Across 324 graded NCAAW games the algo now scales scoring ×1.001 and gives home teams +1.3 points. Team corrections so far: RedHawks attack ×1.040, defense ×0.960 (3 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 50 points), no bet.
